## What problem does this solve?

Currently, different agents and characters perform best with vastly different generation parameters. For instance, a creative roleplay character benefits from a higher temperature to encourage variety, while a structured utility agent (such as a Lorebook Manager, coder, or summarizer) requires a very low temperature (e.g., 0.1 to 0.3) to prevent formatting errors and infinite loops. I suspect that I need to modify the temperature the DRY for my particular model to stop looping when making lorebook entries.

Having to manually change generation settings (temperature, repetition penalty, samplers) for utility agents would be useful for the workflow. 

## Proposed solution

I would like to see the ability to set and modify generation parameters directly within each agent's configuration page or profile sheet. 

Specifically:
- When clicking on an agent/character, a dedicated section or tab should allow users to configure custom parameter overrides (such as Temperature, Repetition Penalty, Max Tokens, or specific samplers).
- These custom settings would automatically override the global settings whenever that specific agent is active or generating a response.

## Summary

When `marinara-server` runs through `docker compose up`, a browser on the same host can fail to use the Remote Runtime URL because the request reaches the container from the Docker bridge gateway IP instead of loopback.

## Expected behavior

A same-machine browser pointed at `http://127.0.0.1:8787` should be able to reach the Docker Compose remote runtime without requiring users to configure LAN-style remote auth for the local Docker bridge path.

## Actual behavior

The runtime treats the Docker bridge gateway client IP, commonly `172.17.0.1`, as non-loopback remote access. The security middleware rejects the request before the CORS layer adds browser-readable headers, so the browser surfaces the failure as a CORS error instead of a clear auth/configuration problem.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Start the remote runtime with `docker compose up --build`.
2. Start the web client with `pnpm dev`.
3. Set the app Remote Runtime URL to `http://127.0.0.1:8787`.
4. Exercise a remote runtime request from the browser client.

## Impact area

- [ ] App shell, navigation, startup, or providers
- [ ] Catalog resources
- [ ] Chat mode
- [ ] Roleplay mode
- [ ] Game mode
- [ ] Shared mode UI
- [ ] Runtime systems: generation, world-state, visuals, tracker, or haptics
- [ ] Professor Mari or shell tools
- [ ] React-free engine behavior, contracts, agents, or capability ports
- [x] Shared API wrapper or remote runtime routing
- [x] Tauri/Rust storage, assets, LLM, integrations, security, imports, or HTTP runtime
- [x] Docs, contributor workflow, or templates

## Environment

- Branch or commit: refactor / Docker Compose remote runtime
- Run mode: Docker runtime plus browser/web client
- OS + version: Windows host observed; likely any Docker Desktop host using bridge gateway routing
- Node + pnpm versions: not specific to the client toolchain
- Rust version, if relevant: not specific to a Rust compiler version
- Remote Runtime URL configured? yes, `http://127.0.0.1:8787`
- Provider, model, or integration, if relevant: not relevant

## Logs, screenshots, or video

Browser reports a CORS-style failure. Runtime-side behavior is an auth rejection before CORS headers are added for the browser response.

## Regression notes

This is a Docker Compose remote-runtime configuration gap on the refactor branch.

## Additional context

The fix should preserve same-machine Docker browser access while avoiding broad unauthenticated exposure on all host interfaces. Compose can enable the Docker bridge auth bypass while binding the published host port to `127.0.0.1`.

## What problem does this solve?

Currently, the search functionality in the Character Cards library (and to a lesser extent, the Lorebook) is very basic and often feels incomplete. For users managing larger collections, finding specific characters or lore entries is difficult because:
- The search is applied globally, making it impossible to restrict queries to specific fields (e.g., searching for a keyword specifically in a character's "Personality" vs. their "Description", "Title", or "Tags").
- There is no control over matching behavior, such as case sensitivity or strict whitespace matching, leading to irrelevant search results.

## Proposed solution

introducing an expandable "Advanced Search" panel or a set of basic filter toggles next to the search bar with the following features:

1. **Search Scope Filters (Where to search):**
   - Checkboxes or toggles to define which card fields are searched:
     - **Title / Name**
     - **Tags**
     - **Genres**
     - **Description**
     - **Personality**
     - **All fields** (Default)

2. **Matching Parameters:**
   - **Case Sensitive:** A toggle to choose whether the search distinguishes between uppercase and lowercase letters.
   - **Match Type / Whitespace Sensitivity:** Options to switch between *Contains* (default), *Exact Match* (respecting exact spaces and characters), and *Starts With / Ends With*.

## Summary

Chat/game surfaces eagerly invoke optional TTS and regex storage commands even when the user has never configured TTS and may not be actively using regex scripts. In CrabNebula DevTools these appeared alongside a stale stream command as long-running rows:

`command: tts_config 19:41:22 1022784.77ms uri: http://ipc.localhost/tts_config`

`command: storage_list 19:41:22 1022784.36ms entity: regex-scripts options: null uri: http://ipc.localhost/storage_list`

The exact reason those two calls remained pending in that session is not yet proven, but the code does prove that visible chat/game UI mounts these reads eagerly rather than gating them behind actual TTS/regex use.

## Expected behavior

Optional systems should avoid unnecessary embedded IPC/storage work:

- TTS config should not be fetched on ordinary message render when TTS has never been enabled or no TTS control/autoplay path is active.
- Regex scripts should not be repeatedly fetched by general chat/game render paths unless an input/output transform actually needs them, or should at least use a stable cache/stale policy appropriate for rarely changing script definitions.
- Any `tts_config` or `storage_list(regex-scripts)` call that is issued should complete quickly or fail visibly; it should not sit in DevTools with an ever-increasing duration.

## Actual behavior

Code inspection shows eager calls from normal UI render paths:

- `useTTSConfig()` calls `ttsApi.config()` with query key `["tts", "config"]`.
- `ChatMessage` calls `useTTSConfig()` while rendering each message's TTS affordance path.
- `useChatTtsAutoplay()` also calls `useTTSConfig()` before checking whether TTS is enabled.
- `useApplyRegex()` calls `useRegexScripts()`, which calls `storageApi.list("regex-scripts")`.
- `ChatInput`, `ChatMessage`, and game narration paths call `useApplyRegex()`, so regex scripts are loaded as part of ordinary mode surfaces.

In the observed session, the corresponding embedded IPC rows were still running for ~17 minutes.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Run the refactor branch in Tauri desktop mode.
2. Open CrabNebula DevTools.
3. Open a chat/roleplay/game surface without configuring TTS.
4. Observe embedded IPC command rows.
5. Note that `tts_config` and `storage_list` for `regex-scripts` can be issued even if TTS has never been used and regex scripts are not being edited.

## Summary

CrabNebula DevTools can show an embedded Tauri `llm_stream_channel` command still running long after the foreground generation appears complete. One observed row was:

`command: llm_stream_channel 19:41:24 1020502.04ms streamid: cd44cadb-80b4-4c63-a472-59491049baee uri: http://ipc.localhost/llm_stream_channel`

Code inspection points at a stuck stream/IPC lifetime rather than a visible generation state problem: the foreground UI can release after persisted generation events, while the shared LLM stream generator still waits for the underlying Tauri command promise to resolve.

## Expected behavior

When a generation finishes, errors, or is cancelled, the embedded Tauri `llm_stream_channel` command should resolve promptly and unregister its stream id. DevTools should not show old LLM stream commands increasing in duration after the user-visible LLM work is done.

## Actual behavior

At least one `llm_stream_channel` command remains pending for ~17 minutes and continues increasing in duration in CrabNebula DevTools after the user considers the LLM generation finished.

The likely failure path from local inspection:

- `src/shared/api/llm-api.ts` marks the JS stream completed only when the channel receives `done` or `error`, but then still awaits the `invokeTauri("llm_stream_channel", ...)` command promise before the async generator fully returns.
- `src-tauri/src/commands/storage/llm.rs` resolves `llm_stream_channel` only when `marinara_llm::stream_events(...)` returns or cancellation fires.
- `src-tauri/crates/llm/src/lib.rs` emits the terminal `done` event only after the provider-specific stream reader returns.
- The provider stream readers consume `response.bytes_stream()` until EOF. They do not appear to enforce an app-side idle/read timeout or always break on provider semantic terminal events such as `[DONE]`.

This leaves two plausible but related ways for the command to outlive the visible generation:

- A provider or compatible endpoint leaves the HTTP stream open after sending enough content, so Rust never emits `done` and the Tauri command stays pending.
- Rust sends a terminal channel event, but the frontend then waits indefinitely at `await command` if the embedded Tauri command promise does not resolve promptly.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Run the refactor branch in Tauri desktop mode.
2. Open CrabNebula DevTools.
3. Start an LLM generation using streaming.
4. Wait until the UI appears to have completed the generation.
5. Inspect IPC command rows for `llm_stream_channel`.

payload.author: Gunterlie
payload.body:
## Summary

The `/api/assets/avatar/` endpoint only serves avatars from `avatars/characters/` but persona and NPC avatars are saved to different subdirectories that the endpoint never looks at. Files are written to locations they can never be served from.

## Expected behavior

Persona and NPC avatars are served correctly via the remote asset endpoint when using a remote runtime, just like character avatars.

## Actual behavior

- Persona avatars are saved to `avatars/personas/` but the endpoint only serves from `avatars/characters/` → 404
- NPC avatars are saved to `avatars/npc/{chat_id}/{name}` → endpoint rejects the subdirectory path entirely → 404
- Not visibly broken in most cases due to base64 `avatarPath` fallback in the DB, but files are written to locations they can never be served from
- Breaks completely for any character where `avatarPath` is not a base64 data URL (e.g. built-in characters referencing `/sprites/...`)

## Steps to reproduce

1. Run Marinara Engine as a remote HTTP backend
2. Connect the Tauri desktop app via Settings → Remote Runtime URL
3. Upload a new persona avatar or use a chat with NPC avatars
4. Observe: avatar loads via base64 fallback (if present), file endpoint returns 404

To confirm directly:
```bash
curl -u user:pass http://<server>:8787/api/assets/avatar/<persona-avatar-filename>
# → 404, file is actually in avatars/personas/ not avatars/characters/
```

## Environment

- Marinara Engine version: Refactor
- Install type: HTTP Docker Backend
- OS + version: Linux server (Docker)

## Additional context

Root cause is in `http_server.rs` — `avatar_asset_path` hardcodes `avatars/characters/`:

```rust
fn avatar_asset_path(state: &AppState, path: &str) -> Result<PathBuf, AppError> {
    let filename = avatar_asset_filename(path)?;
    Ok(state.data_dir.join("avatars").join("characters").join(filename))
}
```

But saves go to different locations depending on type:
- Characters (`persona_avatar_upload`): `avatars/personas/`
- NPCs (`npc_avatar_upload`): `avatars/npc/{chat_id}/{name}`

The NPC case is additionally broken because the path includes a subdirectory (`{chat_id}`) which `avatar_asset_filename` explicitly rejects (contains `/`).

**Why it's not always visible:** `avatarPath` in each record stores a base64 data URL as a fallback. The frontend falls back to this if the file endpoint fails. This masks the issue but means large base64 blobs are embedded in every API response instead of serving files efficiently.

**Possible fixes:**
- Extend `avatar_asset_path` to accept a collection prefix and update the frontend to pass it in the URL (e.g. `/api/assets/avatar/personas/{filename}`)
- Or search across all avatar subdirectories as a fallback

## Template check

payload.title: [Issue]: Remote avatar endpoint only serves character avatars — persona and NPC avatars always 404

## Why load many things when can load less?

App startup still carry big rocks. PR #1711 makes first bonk: AppShell and chat sidebar now load fewer heavy things at boot. Good. But bundle still says: some chunks big, browser chew much code.

Need next lazy-load hunt.

## What cave see

- Startup main chunk after first pass: about `767.77 kB` minified in local build.
- Optional shell things can hide in chunks until user opens them. This good.
- More places likely still load before user needs them.
- Existing issue #1532 tracks broad large chunk strategy.
- Existing issue #1577 tracks manual vendor chunk policy.
- This issue is narrower: find more app-owned lazy-load wins after AppShell first pass.

## Likely next rocks to lift

- Chat settings drawer and timeline action helpers: many tools, probably not all needed at first chat paint.
- Mode surfaces with huge route chunks: make sure only chosen mode pays chosen-mode cost.
- Game and roleplay heavy panels: verify setup/editor/combat/tracker pieces load only when opened.
- Catalog editors and modals: keep create/edit/import/export flows out of startup path.
- Export helpers and zip/transcript code: only load when user actually exports.
- Any remaining broad barrel import that drags whole feature cave into small shell button.

## How know rock moved

- Run `pnpm build` before/after and compare startup `index-*.js` plus route chunks.
- Use Vite output or visualizer to prove import moved out of startup path.
- Smoke app shell: no blank page, chat list works, open optional surface and it still works.
- For native-ish paths, run Tauri QA if change touches Tauri-only behavior.

## Done when

- We can name each new lazy boundary and why it safe.
- Startup chunk shrinks or expensive work moves behind user action.
- Optional UI still opens cleanly on first click.
- No mode boundary mud: chat, roleplay, game keep own stuff.
- No fake fallback. If lazy import fails, app fail honest or show existing error path.

Less load. Less wait. More smooth.

payload.body:
## Summary

Professor Mari sends `tool_choice` to the LLM provider as a JSON **object** (the
modern OpenAI Chat Completions spec form), but LM Studio's local OpenAI-compatible
server rejects the object form entirely — it only accepts string values
(`"none" | "auto" | "required"`). Result: Mari is unusable on LM Studio for any code
or library question (which automatically trigger the forced-tool path).

Surfaced during the Ubuntu re-test of smoke test #1480 (Professor Mari Deeper Pass).

## Steps to reproduce

1. Install and run LM Studio (tested on the latest available version as of 2026-05-30).
2. Load a chat model in LM Studio and start its Local Server (default
   `http://localhost:1234/v1`).
3. In Marinara, create a `custom` connection pointing to LM Studio.
4. Open Professor Mari, select that connection, and ask any "looks like a codebase
   question" prompt (e.g. *"What does `src/app/shell/AppShell.tsx` do?"*).
5. Observe the error rendered in the chat.

## Expected behavior

Mari should either:
- Send a `tool_choice` value that any OpenAI-API-compatible server accepts (e.g. the
  string `"required"`), or
- Detect that the selected provider rejects the object form and fall back gracefully.

In either case the request should complete and Mari should produce a tool-grounded
answer.

## Actual behavior

Mari surfaces this in-chat error (no crash — error handling is correct, only the request
shape is the bug):

```
LLM error: Provider Error: llm_provider_error:
Provider returned HTTP 400 Bad Request:
Invalid tool_choice type: 'object'. Supported string values: none, auto, required
```

## Wire-level evidence

The actual JSON request body Marinara sent to LM Studio (captured from LM Studio's local
server logs):

```json
{
  "max_tokens": 2048,
  "messages": [
    { "role": "system",  "content": "You are Professor Mari... [truncated]" },
    { "role": "user",    "content": "What does src/app/shell/AppShell.tsx do, and where is the sidebar-toggle button defined?" }
  ],
  "model": "qwen3.5-27b-heretic-i1",
  "stream": false,
  "temperature": 0.4,
  "tool_choice": {
    "function": { "name": "search_marinara_code" },
    "type": "function"
  },
  "tools": [
    { "type": "function", "function": { "name": "read_marinara_library",       "parameters": { ... } } },
    { "type": "function", "function": { "name": "search_marinara_code",        "parameters": { ... } } },
    { "type": "function", "function": { "name": "read_marinara_code_file",     "parameters": { ... } } },
    { "type": "function", "function": { "name": "edit_marinara_code_file",     "parameters": { ... } } },
    { "type": "function", "function": { "name": "create_marinara_extension",   "parameters": { ... } } },
    { "type": "function", "function": { "name": "create_marinara_custom_agent","parameters": { ... } } }
  ]
}
```

The `tools` array is fine; LM Studio's complaint is specifically and only about
`tool_choice` being an object rather than a string.

## Code reference

`src-tauri/src/commands/storage/mari.rs:191-201`:

```rust
if !tools.is_empty() && !has_tool_result && looks_like_codebase_question(latest_user) {
    parameters["toolChoice"] = json!({
        "type": "function",
        "function": { "name": "search_marinara_code" }
    });
} else if !tools.is_empty() && !has_tool_result && looks_like_library_question(latest_user) {
    parameters["toolChoice"] = json!({
        "type": "function",
        "function": { "name": "read_marinara_library" }
    });
}
```

Both branches hardcode the object form. There's no fall-through path that would send
the string form, and no per-provider knowledge that LM Studio only accepts strings.

## Suggested fix directions

Pick one:

1. **Send `tool_choice: "required"` always.** Simplest. Cost: Marinara loses its ability
   to *force a specific* tool — the model picks from the registered tools list. For the
   single-tool-registered case this is equivalent. For Mari's 6-tool registry, the system
   prompt already guid
payload.title: Marinara sends OpenAI object-form tool_choice that LM Studio rejects (HTTP 400)

## Summary

The Agent editor's "Save & close" path closes the editor even when the async save fails. This hides the user's unsaved edits immediately after showing the save failure state.

## Expected behavior

If the agent save fails, the editor should stay open with the user's unsaved edits visible and a clear error message.

## Actual behavior

`handleSave` catches the failed `updateAgent.mutateAsync` call and sets `saveError`, but the "Save & close" click handler calls `closeAgentDetail()` afterward anyway. That unmounts the editor despite the failed save.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open an agent on the refactor branch.
2. Edit the agent so the unsaved warning appears.
3. Click Back.
4. Click "Save & close" while `updateAgent.mutateAsync` fails.

## Summary

The preset editor's "Save & close" action closes the editor immediately after starting an async save, before the save succeeds. If the save is pending or fails, the UI can make it look like the user's changes were accepted while hiding the edited content.

## Summary

The chat content's vertical scrollbar **renders through the Tracker Panel** — the
scrollbar track and thumb paint on top of the tracker panel cards instead of being
properly clipped to the chat container or moved to its visible width.

Surfaced during the Ubuntu re-test of smoke test #1479.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Enable the Tracker Panel in Settings → Appearance.
2. Open a Roleplay chat with enough message history to force a scrollbar.
3. From the Roleplay HUD, click **Show Tracker Panel** (configure it on the same side as
   the scrollbar — typically right).
4. Scroll the chat. Observe the right edge where the tracker panel sits.

## Expected behavior

The chat scrollbar should either:
- Render only within the visible width of the chat container (so it sits to the *left* of
  the tracker panel), **or**
- Be visually clipped by the tracker panel's stacking context so it doesn't paint on top
  of tracker cards.

## Actual behavior

The scrollbar (track and thumb) paints **on top of** the tracker panel cards as a thin
vertical line cutting through them.

## Code reference

The tracker panel sits at `position: fixed` with `z-30` (per `AppShell.tsx` tracker
panel render block, ~line 845 onward). The chat scrolling container uses native browser
overflow scrolling, and the scrollbar gutter is positioned at the chat's full layout
width — which extends beneath the fixed tracker.

## Suggested fix direction

Either:
- Apply `scrollbar-gutter: stable` and constrain the scroll container's `right` edge to
  stop at the tracker panel's leading edge, so the scrollbar renders in the visible chat
  area, or
- Increase the tracker panel's effective stacking context (e.g. enforce it as the
  topmost child of a clipping parent) so the scrollbar is occluded.

The first option is preferable because it preserves scrollbar usability — the second
hides the scrollbar behind the tracker, which is also bad UX.

## Environment

- Marinara Engine branch: `refactor` @ `5ea8a10c`
- OS: Ubuntu (Wayland)
- GPU: NVIDIA RTX 5060 Ti
- Run mode: Tauri desktop (`pnpm tauri dev`)
- WebKitGTK 2.52.3 (note: native scrollbar rendering on GTK may make this more visually
  obvious than on macOS/Windows webviews, where overlay scrollbars are more common)

## Screenshot

The thin vertical pink/purple line running down the right edge of the chat area —
visible cutting through the "WORLD" tracker section and continuing through "Living room"
into the start of "PRESENT CHARACTERS" — is the chat scrollbar painting on top of the
tracker cards.

![Scrollbar bleeds through tracker panel](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aeriondyseti/Marinara-Engine/evidence/smoke-1479-ubuntu/pr-evidence/smoke-1479-ubuntu/scrollbar-through-tracker-panel.png)

## Related

- Smoke test: #1479 (Ubuntu re-test)
- Sibling layout bug filed separately: tracker panel overlays chat content when sidebars
  are open.
payload.title: Chat scrollbar renders through Tracker Panel (z-ordering / scrollbar-gutter)

payload.body:
## Summary

In Game mode, the HUD widget cards are laid out in a vertical flex stack. Because
they share normal document flow, **collapsing or dragging one card reflows all the
others** — collapse a widget and everything below it jumps up; drag one and the
stack shifts. This makes the HUD feel unstable during play.

Additionally, dragging a widget by its header also fires the header's click
handler on pointer-up, so **repositioning a panel toggles its collapsed state**
as an unwanted side effect.

## Proposed fix

Render the widget cards as independently positioned floating panels:

- A `FloatingWidgetStack` measures each card's natural flow position once (via
  `useLayoutEffect`, before paint — no flicker), then pins each card to
  `position: absolute` at its measured top. From then on a card's height changes
  (collapse/expand) affect only that card; neighbours don't move.
- Re-measure only when the visible set changes (add/remove/reorder), never on
  collapse — so a minimised card leaves its slot open instead of yanking the
  others up.
- Distinguish a drag from a click on the header (flag set on `onDragStart`,
  swallowed on the trailing `onClick`) so repositioning no longer toggles
  collapse.

## Scope

Single file: `src/features/modes/game/components/GameWidgetPanel.tsx`.
Typecheck and lint clean.
payload.title: Game HUD widgets reflow when one is collapsed or dragged; dragging toggles collapse

## What problem does this solve?

Refactor desktop builds currently have a manual update handoff: the app can check GitHub releases and open the release page, but it does not install updates automatically. That is acceptable for pre-alpha testing, but stable refactor releases need an explicit product/release decision so users know whether Marinara will continue with manual releases or support signed automatic desktop updates.

Without a tracked decision, future installer/update problems can keep landing as old-codebase launcher bugs or vague "proper updater" requests instead of a clear refactor release/distribution plan.

## Proposed behavior

Decide and document the stable refactor update strategy before stable refactor desktop releases ship.

The decision should cover:

- Whether stable refactor desktop builds remain manual-release only or use signed Tauri updater support.
- Which platforms are in scope for automatic updates: Windows, macOS, Linux, or a subset.
- Who owns updater signing keys/secrets and where release metadata is published.
- Whether GitHub Releases are the update metadata/source of truth or whether a separate update endpoint is needed.
- What the in-app update UI should say for supported, unsupported, pre-alpha, and manual-only builds.
- What recovery path users should follow if an update fails.

If signed automatic updates are chosen, follow-up implementation tickets should be split by release surface/platform rather than handled as one broad PR.

## Expected owner or impact area

- [x] App shell, navigation, startup, or providers
- [ ] Catalog resources: chats, characters, personas, lorebooks, presets, connections, agents, gallery, or knowledge
- [ ] Chat mode
- [ ] Roleplay mode
- [ ] Game mode
- [ ] Shared mode UI
- [ ] Runtime systems: generation, world-state, visuals, tracker, or haptics
- [ ] Professor Mari or shell tools
- [ ] React-free engine behavior, contracts, agents, or capability ports
- [x] Shared API wrapper or remote runtime routing
- [x] Tauri/Rust storage, assets, LLM, integrations, security, imports, or HTTP runtime
- [x] Docs, contributor workflow, or templates

## Refactor branch considerations

Current refactor behavior is intentionally manual:

- #1374 added `update_check` / `update_apply` and Settings > Advanced controls that open the release page instead of installing updates.
- #1377 added manual pre-alpha platform builds and explicitly disables updater metadata for pre-alpha artifacts.
- The current Tauri config does not include updater plugin configuration, updater endpoints, updater public keys, or updater artifacts.

Tauri updater support would require release/distribution work, not just a UI change: plugin dependency/config, signed artifacts, updater public key configuration, private key custody, update endpoint/metadata publication, platform-specific bundle behavior, and failure recovery copy.

## Alternatives considered

Keep manual releases indefinitely and make the in-app update UI/docs clearer. This is simpler and avoids signing/secrets/update-metadata maintenance, but users still have to download and install releases themselves.

Do nothing for now and keep relying on pre-alpha warnings. That is fine for pre-alpha builds, but it leaves the stable refactor release path undecided.

## Additional context

Related old-codebase report: #1671.

Related refactor work:

- #1348 tracked the missing refactor update check/apply surface.
- #1374 restored a bounded manual-release update handoff.
- #1368 tracked desktop build/distribution parity.
- #1377 added manual pre-alpha platform builds.
- #1384 fixed follow-up pre-alpha build failures.

payload.author: aeriondyseti
payload.body:
## Summary

Reopening a chat that has persisted Echo Chamber results crashes the **entire** app
with an uncaught `TypeError`. Because there is no root-level error boundary, the
crash unmounts the whole React tree, leaving an empty `#root` — which on the
frameless (`decorations: false`) Tauri window presents as a **solid-colour,
frozen, un-draggable window with no visible error**.

This is a deterministic data-contract bug, not environment- or state-specific.
Any user who has run the `echo-chamber` agent and then reloads/reopens that chat
will hit it.

## The error

```
TypeError: undefined is not an object (evaluating 'msg.characterName.length')
  at EchoChamberPanel.tsx  (nameColorMap useMemo)
```

## Root cause

There are **two independent defects** that compound:

### Bug A — reload path deserializes the wrong shape (the crash)

Echo runs are persisted as `agent-runs` rows whose payload is nested:

```jsonc
{
  "resultType": "echo_message",
  "resultData": {
    "reactions": [
      { "characterName": "…", "reaction": "…" }
    ]
  }
}
```

(Confirmed against real on-disk data: 26/26 echo rows use this nested shape.)

- The **live SSE path** reads it correctly — `use-generate.ts:680-686` flattens
  `data.reactions[]` and calls `addEchoMessage(characterName, text)`.
- The **reload path** does NOT. `EchoChamberPanel.tsx:122` asserts a flat shape:

  ```ts
  storageApi.list<{ characterName: string; reaction: string; timestamp: number }>("agent-runs", …)
  ```

  The row has no top-level `characterName` (it's two levels down in
  `resultData.reactions[]`), so every `msg.characterName` is `undefined`, and
  `nameColorMap`'s `msg.characterName.length` throws.

The `list<T>()` generic is an **unchecked cast**, so `tsc` validated a shape that
never exists on disk. The crash only surfaces with real persisted data, which is
why it passes typecheck and a clean profile but dies on any profile with echo
history.

### Bug B — no root error boundary (severity multiplier)

The only error boundary in `src/` is inside `EncounterModal`. A single component
throw therefore takes down the whole app *silently*. Turning a localized data bug
into "the entire window is dead and shows nothing" is the actual reason this was
so hard to diagnose.

## Proposed fix

1. **Bug A:** make the reload path flatten `resultData.reactions[]` exactly like
   `use-generate.ts` does, ideally extracting a single shared parser
   (`parseMaybeRecord`/`readString` already exist) so the two readers can't drift
   again. Correct the `list<T>()` type to the real stored shape.
2. **Bug B:** add a root-level error boundary above `App` that renders the error
   instead of unmounting to a blank screen.
3. Consider parsing/validating (e.g. Zod) at the storage I/O boundary rather than
   asserting shapes via generics, to kill this defect class.

## Repro

1. Use a profile that has run the Echo Chamber agent (has `echo_message` rows in
   `agent-runs`).
2. Reopen that chat (or reload the app).
3. App renders briefly, then goes blank/frozen.

## Environment

Surfaced under `pnpm tauri dev` (WebKitGTK). Not WebKitGTK-specific — it also
throws in a plain browser when echo rows are present; the blank-window
*presentation* is specific to the frameless Tauri window.
payload.title: Echo Chamber reload crashes entire app (blank/frozen window) — wrong deserialization shape + no root error boundary

## What problem does this solve?

The refactor branch currently has a useful architecture-focused ESLint setup, but broader JavaScript, TypeScript, and React diagnostics are not restored yet. A direct enablement of recommended rules is too noisy to make CI-blocking immediately, so the project needs a staged restoration path that preserves the existing architecture guard while making general lint signal reproducible and actionable.

## Proposed behavior

Restore useful ESLint coverage in staged PRs:

1. Keep the current architecture lint gate blocking.
2. Add a reproducible non-blocking full ESLint report path for recommended JavaScript/TypeScript/React diagnostics.
3. Remove fake `no-undef` noise from browser, DOM, TypeScript, and Node globals before judging remaining findings.
4. Add TypeScript ESLint recommended rules in warning/report-only mode first.
5. Restore React Hooks signal, starting with `rules-of-hooks` and then triaging `exhaustive-deps`.
6. Work through unused variables and smaller recommended-rule buckets by owner area.
7. Promote clean rule buckets into CI enforcement only after the report is understood and stable.

## Expected owner or impact area

- [ ] App shell, navigation, startup, or providers
- [ ] Catalog resources: chats, characters, personas, lorebooks, presets, connections, agents, gallery, or knowledge
- [ ] Chat mode
- [ ] Roleplay mode
- [ ] Game mode
- [ ] Shared mode UI
- [ ] Runtime systems: generation, world-state, visuals, tracker, or haptics
- [ ] Professor Mari or shell tools
- [ ] React-free engine behavior, contracts, agents, or capability ports
- [ ] Shared API wrapper or remote runtime routing
- [ ] Tauri/Rust storage, assets, LLM, integrations, security, imports, or HTTP runtime
- [x] Docs, contributor workflow, or templates

## Refactor branch considerations

This should be a tooling-first effort. Do not copy the old legacy client ESLint config wholesale; the refactor tree has different ownership boundaries. Preserve the current architecture rules in `eslint.config.js`, keep CI behavior unchanged until each bucket is intentionally ratcheted, and avoid deleting exported contracts, schemas, generated shapes, or extension/API surfaces just because an early unused-variable report flags them.

## Alternatives considered

Enabling all recommended rules as a blocking lint gate immediately would create a large noisy failure surface and obscure the real signal. Leaving lint architecture-only forever would miss TypeScript, React Hooks, and local cleanup diagnostics that can catch real regressions.

## Additional context

Initial local investigation found the current architecture-focused ESLint config clean, while a temporary recommended-rule overlay produced thousands of findings mostly dominated by false `no-undef` noise and unused variables. The first PR should be config-only: reproducible reports and direct lint dependencies if needed, without changing runtime behavior or CI gates.

payload.body: ## Summary Character avatars in the chat list (Convo / RP / GM) render broken. The avatar `` resolves to a Tauri asset-protocol URL like `http://asset.localhost/<...>/com.marinara-engine.app/avatars/.png`, but the request returns HTTP 404, so `naturalWidth` is 0 and a broken-image fragment shows instead of the portrait. ## Evidence (refactor HEAD, `pnpm tauri dev`, Windows) - `RecentChats.tsx` renders ``. The resolved src for an affected character is e.g. `http://asset.localhost/C:\Users\\AppData\Roaming\com.marinara-engine.app\avatars\.png`. - `fetch()` of that URL returns `status=404`; the `` reports `complete=true`, `naturalWidth=0`. - The app-data bundle `%APPDATA%\com.marinara-engine.app\` contains `backgrounds`, `data`, `fonts`, `game-assets` but **no `avatars/` directory**, while ~30 character records reference `avatars/.png`. - The crop style is correct (`getAvatarCropStyle` emits a normal `100% × 119.79%`), and game-mode sprites + bundled icons load fine. Only the `asset.localhost` character-avatar files 404. ## Two parts 1. **Missing-file resilience (clear gap):** `RecentChats.tsx` renders the `` whenever `avatarUrl` is truthy, with no `onError` fallback. A 404/missing avatar should fall back to the name-initial placeholder (already implemented for the no-avatar case) instead of showing a broken image. This is worth fixing regardless of why the file is missing. 2. **Root cause of the 404 (needs triage):** either the avatar binaries were never written to this bundle's `avatars/` dir, or the write path and read path disagree. Read path: `src/features/catalog/characters/lib/character-avatar-url.ts` -> `src/shared/api/local-file-api` (asset protocol). Write path: `src-tauri/src/commands/storage/avatars.rs`. Avatar loading was last touched by #1590. ## Impact Every character avatar whose file is absent from `avatars/` renders as a broken image across the chat list (and anywhere `characterAvatarUrl` is used), rather than degrading to the initial.

payload.author: Gunterlie
payload.body:
# feat: make TTS voice-lookup path configurable per provider

## Summary

Marinara hardcodes `/audio/voices` as the path for OpenAI-compatible voice discovery. Servers that implement an OpenAI-style TTS API but expose their voice list under a different path (e.g. `/v1/voices`, `/voices`, or a completely custom route) cannot be used for voice lookup without forking the binary. Adding a single `voicesPath` config field — defaulting to `/audio/voices` — unblocks every such server at zero cost to users who never change the default.

**OpenAI's official API does not define a voice-listing endpoint at all. Their TTS voices (alloy, echo, fable, onyx, nova, shimmer) are documented as a fixed enum — there is no published `GET /audio/voices` route in the OpenAI spec. The path `/audio/voices` is a de-facto convention adopted by OpenAI-compatible servers (LocalAI and others), not an OpenAI standard. Because there is no standard, implementations vary — making the path hardcoded is the wrong default.**

## Expected behavior

A user running a custom or self-hosted OpenAI-compatible TTS server can enter the path their server uses for voice listing (e.g. `/voices`) in the TTS settings. Marinara uses that path instead of the hardcoded one. Users who leave the field blank get the current behavior unchanged.

## Actual behavior

The voices path is hardcoded in `openai_voices_url()`:

```rust
// src-tauri/src/commands/storage/integrations/tts.rs, line 489
fn openai_voices_url(base: &str, model: Option<&str>) -> String {
    let raw_url = format!("{base}/audio/voices");  // ← not configurable
    ...
}
```

Any server that exposes its voice catalog under a different path returns a 404 or an unexpected response. Marinara falls back to a static hardcoded list and the user sees no provider voices — with no indication of why.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Configure a custom OpenAI-compatible TTS server whose voice endpoint is `GET /v1/voices` (no `/audio/` segment)
2. Enter its base URL in TTS settings
3. Open the voice picker — only the built-in fallback list appears, not the server's voices
4. Server logs show a 404 for `GET /v1/audio/voices`

## Environment

- Marinara Engine version: Refactor branch
- Affected providers: all OpenAI-compatible sources (`source: "openai"`, NanoGPT, and any custom `baseUrl`)
- Not affected: ElevenLabs (uses its own dedicated path), PocketTTS (no live lookup)

## Proposed fix

**Part A — Add `voicesPath` to the TTS config schema**

New optional field, validated the same way as `baseUrl` (trimmed, leading slash normalized). Empty string = use the default.

**Part B — Read `voicesPath` in `openai_voices_url()`**

```rust
// src-tauri/src/commands/storage/integrations/tts.rs
fn openai_voices_url(base: &str, model: Option<&str>, voices_path: &str) -> String {
    let path = voices_path.trim().trim_start_matches('/');
    let path = if path.is_empty() { "audio/voices" } else { path };
    let raw_url = format!("{base}/{path}");
    let Ok(mut url) = reqwest::Url::parse(&raw_url) else {
        return raw_url;
    };
    if let Some(model) = model.map(str::trim).filter(|v| !v.is_empty()) {
        url.query_pairs_mut().append_pair("model", model);
    }
    url.to_string()
}
```

**Part C — Expose `voicesPath` in `TTSConfigCard`**

Add a text input below the existing `baseUrl` field. Placeholder: `/audio/voices`. Only shown when `source` is `"openai"` or a custom provider (hide for ElevenLabs and PocketTTS, which have fixed paths).

**Part D — Persist via `tts_config` mutation**

`voicesPath` gets written and read through the existing `"app-settings"` / `"tts"` store — no new storage key required.

## Scope

- One new config key (`voicesPath`)
- One changed function signature (`openai_voices_url` gains a `voices_path: &str` parameter)
- One new UI input in `TTSConfigCard.tsx`
- No changes to ElevenLabs, PocketTTS

## Template check

- [ ] I DID NOT read this template and provide the requested details.
payload.title: [Issue] feat: make TTS voice-lookup path configurable per provider

payload.body: ## Summary The connections sidebar behaves incorrectly during resize — content squishes, squashes, and the resize feels sluggish. No other right-side panel has this problem. ## Expected behavior Resize feels instant and smooth, content reflows cleanly like CharactersPanel or LorebooksPanel. ## Actual behavior - Content squishes/squashes visually while dragging the resize handle - Resize feels sluggish compared to all other right-side panels ## Steps to reproduce 1. Open the Connections sidebar 2. Drag the resize handle left and right 3. Compare to Characters or Lorebooks sidebar — those resize cleanly ## Environment - Marinara Engine version: Refactor - Install type: MacOS App from Source <---> HTTP Docker Backend on Ubuntu - OS + version: macOS (Tauri) + Linux server (Docker/web) ## Additional context Two root causes, both unique to ConnectionsPanel: **1. framer-motion `Reorder` layout animations (the squish)** ConnectionsPanel is the only right-side panel using `Reorder.Group` / `Reorder.Item` (for folder drag-to-reorder). ## Summary

All character search and filtering (by name, tags, creator) is done client-side via `Array.filter()` after the full collection has been fetched. The Rust storage backend supports only exact-match filters, not substring search. This means the user cannot search until the entire payload has arrived and been parsed — at 180 characters with the avatar fix in place that is ~144 KB; at 1000+ characters it becomes a bottleneck again. Adding a `search` parameter to the backend list endpoint enables search-as-you-type with no full-dataset download.

## Expected behavior

Typing in a character search box returns results immediately, without requiring the full collection to be in memory first. Works at any collection size.

## Actual behavior

- Opening a picker with 180+ characters: the full collection downloads, then `useMemo` filters it client-side
- Searching is fast once data is cached, but the first load always blocks on the full fetch
- At 1000+ characters the in-memory filter pass itself becomes noticeable

## Steps to reproduce

1. Have 500+ characters
2. Open the character picker in ChatSetupWizard
3. Type a search term immediately — results are blocked until the full list loads
4. After the first load, search is fast (React Query cache)

## Environment

- Marinara Engine version: Refactor
- Install type: MacOS App from Source <---> HTTP Docker Backend on Ubuntu
- OS + version: macOS (Tauri) + Linux server (Docker/web)

## Additional context

### Current backend capability

`src-tauri/src/commands/storage/commands/entities.rs` line 61:

```rust
// Only supports exact-match filters (AND-ed together)
(_, Some(filters)) if !filters.is_empty() => state.storage.list_where(&entity, filters)?,
```

No substring match, no full-text search.

### Proposed backend change

Add a `search` field to the options object in `storage_list`. Implement as a case-insensitive substring match on `data.name` (SQLite `LIKE '%term%'`). Optionally extend to tags and creator. SQLite LIKE on an indexed column handles <10k records without FTS5.

```rust
// entities.rs — additive, optional param
if let Some(search) = options.get("search").and_then(Value::as_str) {
    rows.retain(|row| {
        row.get("data")
            .and_then(|d| d.get("name"))
            .and_then(Value::as_str)
            .map(|name| name.to_lowercase().contains(&search.to_lowercase()))
            .unwrap_or(false)
    });
}
```

### Frontend change

Pass the debounced search term as a query param. React Query includes it in the query key so each distinct search has its own cache entry:

```ts
useQuery({
  queryKey: ["characters", "summaries", { q: searchTerm }],
  queryFn: () => storageApi.list("characters", {
    ...CHARACTER_SUMMARY_OPTIONS,
    search: searchTerm,
  }),
  enabled: searchTerm.length > 0,
})
```

Empty search (browse all) continues to use the existing cached full list — no change to that path.

### Constraint: local Tauri install keeps working

The `search` param goes through the same `storageApi` / `invoke` abstraction. No HTTP-only assumptions. Callers that omit `search` get current behavior unchanged.

### Dependency

This issue is independent of issues #1–#3 but is most useful after #1 (avatar payload) is fixed, since before that the per-query network cost dominates regardless of search.

---

>
> **Related issues:** #1582 #1583 #1584

## Summary

`ChatSidebar` and `LorebooksPanel` call `useCharacterSummaries()` to load the entire character collection at startup, when in practice each only needs data for a small fixed set of characters. `ChatSidebar` only displays avatars/names for characters in active recent chats (3–10 records). `LorebooksPanel` only needs an ID→name map for characters already linked to a lorebook. The fix requires no backend changes.

## Expected behavior

Sidebar and lorebook panels load their character data instantly without pulling the full collection.

## Actual behavior

- On app startup, `ChatSidebar` triggers a full `useCharacterSummaries()` fetch — after issue #1 is fixed this is 144 KB; today it is 315 MB
- `LorebooksPanel` does the same to build a name lookup map for a handful of linked characters
- These fetches share the React Query cache with pickers, but they cause the cache to be populated immediately on startup rather than on first use

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open the app
2. DevTools → Network → observe `storage_list` for `characters` firing on startup, before any character picker is opened
3. Check the caller — it originates from `ChatSidebar` mounting in the shell

## Environment

- Marinara Engine version: Refactor
- Install type: MacOS App from Source <---> HTTP Docker Backend on Ubuntu
- OS + version: macOS (Tauri) + Linux server (Docker/web)

## Additional context

### Affected components

| Component | File | Line | Fetches | Needs |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ChatSidebar` | `src/app/shell/ChatSidebar.tsx` | 135 | All characters | Names/avatars for ~3–10 active chat characters |
| `LorebooksPanel` | `src/features/catalog/lorebooks/components/LorebooksPanel.tsx` | 92 | All characters | ID→name map for linked characters only |
| `LorebookEditor` | `src/features/catalog/lorebooks/components/LorebookEditor.tsx` | 311 | All characters | ID→name map for linked characters only |

### Fix

**ChatSidebar** — replace full fetch with `byIds`:

```ts
// before
const { data: allCharacters } = useCharacterSummaries();

// after — only fetch the characters that appear in recent chats
const { data: allCharacters } = useCharacterSummariesByIds(recentChatCharacterIds);
```

**LorebooksPanel / LorebookEditor** — same pattern, using the character IDs already present in the lorebook's linked character list.

This means `useCharacterSummaries()` is no longer called on startup — the full collection is only fetched when a user explicitly opens a picker or the character library.

## Summary

`CharacterLibraryView` and `CharactersPanel` map every character directly to DOM nodes with no windowing. At 200 characters there are 200 full card elements in the DOM at once. Additionally, both components call `useCharacters()` (full records) instead of `useCharacterSummaries()`, fetching fields like `description`, `personality`, and `scenario` that are never displayed in a list card. Neither issue requires backend changes.

## Expected behavior

The library grid and sidebar panel scroll smoothly at any collection size. Only visible cards exist in the DOM.

## Actual behavior

- Scrolling through a large character library is sluggish — layout and paint time grows linearly with collection size
- Initial render blocks the main thread while 200+ card components mount simultaneously
- `useCharacters()` fetches `description`, `personality`, `scenario`, `first_mes`, and `alternate_greetings` (~10 KB per character) that are unused in list context

## Steps to reproduce

1. Have 150+ characters
2. Navigate to the Character Library tab
3. Open DevTools → Performance → record
4. Scroll through the list
5. Observe long tasks in the scripting lane on mount and during scroll

## Environment

- Marinara Engine version: Refactor
- Install type: MacOS App from Source <---> HTTP Docker Backend on Ubuntu
- OS + version: macOS (Tauri) + Linux server (Docker/web)

## Additional context

### Affected files

| File | Line | Issue |
|---|---|---|
| `src/features/catalog/characters/components/CharacterLibraryView.tsx` | 201 | `useCharacters()` — full records |
| `src/features/catalog/characters/components/CharacterLibraryView.tsx` | 400 | `sortedCharacters.map(...)` — no windowing |
| `src/features/catalog/characters/components/CharactersPanel.tsx` | 115 | `useCharacters()` — full records |

`@tanstack/react-virtual` is not currently installed. No virtualization library is present in `package.json`.

### Fix

**Part A — Switch to summaries**

```ts
// CharacterLibraryView.tsx line 201 — before
const { data: characters } = useCharacters();

// after
const { data: characters } = useCharacterSummaries();
```

Same change in `CharactersPanel.tsx` line 115. Full record data is only needed in the detail/editor view, not the list.

**Part B — Virtualize the grid and list**

Install `@tanstack/react-virtual` and wrap the `sortedCharacters.map(...)` in `CharacterLibraryView` and the list in `CharactersPanel` with a virtualizer. Only ~30 DOM nodes exist at any time regardless of collection size.

Note: after issue #1 (avatar payload fix) is merged, avatar images will be real URLs and `loading="lazy"` will apply — virtualization then means only visible cards ever request their avatar image.

## Summary

Every character list fetch transfers the full base64-encoded avatar image for every character inside the JSON payload. With 182 characters this is a 300 MB transfer taking ~12 seconds before any UI can render. Removing `avatarPath` from list queries drops the payload to 144 KB and 0.35 seconds — a 2,180× reduction.

## Expected behavior

Character pickers and the library open in well under one second. Avatar images load per-card, on demand, only when visible.

## Actual behavior

Measured against a live server with 182 characters:

| Query | Payload | Time |
|---|---|---|
| Full records (`useCharacters`) | 319 MB | 11.9 s |
| Summary incl. `avatarPath` (`useCharacterSummaries`) | 315 MB | 11.9 s |
| Summary without `avatarPath` | **144 KB** | **0.35 s** |

Per-character breakdown:
```
avatarPath:   ~1,168,304 bytes  (base64 data URI — the full image)
data.*:             ~629 bytes  (name, tags, extensions)
id + comment:        ~25 bytes
```

169 of 182 characters store their avatar as `data:image/png;base64,...` directly in the record. Because `avatarPath` starts with `data:`, `getCharacterAvatarLoadingMode` returns `'eager'` — lazy loading provides zero relief.

The field-selection optimization in `CHARACTER_SUMMARY_OPTIONS` has no effect because `avatarPath` is one of the selected fields.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Import 150+ characters with avatar images
2. Open DevTools → Network → filter by `invoke`
3. Start a new chat — observe the `storage_list` POST response is hundreds of MB
4. Note time from click to list becoming interactive (~12 s on a remote server)

## Environment

- Marinara Engine version: Refactor
- Install type: MacOS App from Source <---> HTTP Docker Backend on Ubuntu
- OS + version: macOS (Tauri) + Linux server (Docker/web)

## Additional context

### Root cause

`avatarPath` in `CHARACTER_SUMMARY_OPTIONS` is a precomputed `data:image/png;base64,...` string, not a file path:

```ts
// src/features/catalog/characters/hooks/use-characters.ts
const CHARACTER_SUMMARY_OPTIONS = {
  fields: ["id", "data", "comment", "avatarPath"],  // ← ~1 MB per character
  fieldSelections: { data: ["name", "tags", "extensions"] }
}
```

The backend already stores the avatar as a file and exposes its path via `avatarFilePath` and `avatarFilename` fields (verified in full record responses).

The existing `/api/assets/:kind/*path` HTTP endpoint serves backgrounds, fonts, and lorebook images but does not yet support `avatar` as a kind.

### Fix (three parts, one PR)

**Part A — Remove `avatarPath` from list queries**

```ts
const CHARACTER_SUMMARY_OPTIONS = {
  fields: ["id", "data", "comment", "avatarFilename"],  // swap avatarPath → avatarFilename
  fieldSelections: { data: ["name", "tags", "extensions"] }
}
```

**Part B — Add avatar file serving endpoint**

Add one match arm to `managed_asset_path` in `src-tauri/src/http_server.rs`:

```rust
"avatar" => Ok(state.avatars_dir.join(path)),
```

This exposes `/api/assets/avatar/{filename}` for remote/web deployments.

**Part C — Update `CharacterAvatarImage` to load from URL**

```ts
// Remote / web:
const src = `/api/assets/avatar/${avatarFilename}`

// Local Tauri (keeps working unchanged):
const src = convertFileSrc(avatarFilePath)
```

Because `src` is now a URL rather than a data URI, the browser uses `loading="lazy"` — avatars only load when a card scrolls into view.

### Constraint: local Tauri install keeps working

`convertFileSrc` is the standard Tauri utility for turning filesystem paths into webview-loadable URLs. It is already used elsewhere in the codebase. No IPC changes are required.

---

> This is part of a series of related performance issues (#1 of 4). 
>
> **Related issues:** #1583 #1584 #1585

The repo also has a configured `size-limit` CSS budget of 250 kB for `dist/assets/*.css`, so the current main CSS size needs either reduction or an explicit budget decision.

## What problem does this solve?

`vite.config.ts` currently has no `build.rollupOptions.output.manualChunks` policy. After feature-level eager imports are cleaned up, the startup bundle may still be noisy because framework and vendor modules are grouped into the entry chunk by default.

Current startup entry vendor contributors include:

- React DOM client production build;
- Zod;
- Tailwind Merge;
- `@dnd-kit/core`;
- DOMPurify;
- Motion/Framer Motion internals;
- Sonner;
- Tauri window API.

Without an explicit chunk policy, the warning remains ambient and it is harder to tell whether a future warning is framework cost, feature leakage, or a real regression.

## Proposed behavior

Define a small, intentional manual chunk policy in `vite.config.ts` after the eager feature import fixes are handled.

The policy should prefer stable, cache-friendly groups instead of many tiny chunks. Candidate groups:

- React/framework runtime;
- query/state/runtime utilities;
- large UI support libraries such as motion, drag-and-drop, sanitizer, and toast;
- Tauri/browser runtime helpers where useful.

Also decide whether to document or raise `build.chunkSizeWarningLimit` only after the remaining large chunks are intentional.

## Expected owner or impact area

- [x] App shell, navigation, startup, or providers
- [ ] Catalog resources: chats, characters, personas, lorebooks, presets, connections, agents, gallery, or knowledge
- [ ] Chat mode
- [ ] Roleplay mode
- [ ] Game mode
- [x] Shared mode UI
- [ ] Runtime systems: generation, world-state, visuals, tracker, or haptics
- [ ] Professor Mari or shell tools
- [ ] React-free engine behavior, contracts, agents, or capability ports
- [ ] Shared API wrapper or remote runtime routing
- [ ] Tauri/Rust storage, assets, LLM, integrations, security, imports, or HTTP runtime
- [x] Docs, contributor workflow, or templates

## Refactor branch considerations

This should not change product behavior. Keep the chunk policy boring and reviewable; avoid using `chunkSizeWarningLimit` alone as the fix unless maintainers explicitly decide the current bundle shape is acceptable.

Acceptance checks:

- `pnpm build` passes.
- The build output has intentional framework/vendor chunks instead of one monolithic startup entry.
- The Vite large chunk warning is gone, or any remaining warning is documented with a clear threshold decision.
- Route and panel lazy chunks still load correctly in Tauri desktop.

## Alternatives considered

Raising `chunkSizeWarningLimit` first would quiet the warning but would not improve cacheability or make future feature leakage visible.

## Additional context

This is one implementation slice under #1532 and should probably come after the startup import and background autonomous slices.

## What problem does this solve?

The AppShell-level background autonomous poller currently imports generation/runtime modules at startup even though background generation only runs after the poller finds an eligible inactive conversation chat.

`src/features/modes/conversation/hooks/autonomous/use-background-autonomous.ts` imports these at module load:

- `startGeneration` from `src/engine/generation/start-generation.ts`
- autonomous chat services from `src/engine/modes/chat/autonomous/autonomous.service.ts`
- `llmApi`, `storageApi`, and `integrationGateway`
- catalog/chat query helpers via broad barrels

Rollup metadata for the startup entry includes generation modules such as `start-generation.ts`, `prompt-assembly.ts`, `agent-runner.ts`, `agent-executor.ts`, and game prompt helpers. That keeps the main entry large before any background autonomous generation is actually needed.

## Proposed behavior

Keep the polling hook small at startup and dynamically import a focused background autonomous runtime only when generation is about to run.

The startup hook should be able to:

- schedule and cancel polling;
- inspect the minimal chat metadata needed to decide whether a background generation may be needed;
- lazy-load the generation runner only after an eligible inactive conversation passes the preflight checks.

The lazy runtime can own `startGeneration`, provider/runtime adapters, prompt assembly, notification side effects, and query invalidation after generation completes.

- [x] App shell, navigation, startup, or providers

Acceptance checks:

- `pnpm build` passes.
- The startup entry no longer includes `src/engine/generation/start-generation.ts`, `src/engine/generation/prompt-assembly.ts`, or `src/engine/agents-runtime/executor/agent-executor.ts` solely because the background autonomous poller is mounted.

`pnpm build` still emits the Vite large chunk warning. Rollup module metadata shows the startup entry includes heavy game, shared chat UI, and catalog/chat modules that should stay behind lazy route or panel boundaries.

## What problem does this solve?

Heavy profile import/export still has a scaling and data-contract risk after the immediate #1511 fix. Marinara profiles are still conceptually treated as one monolithic `marinara-profile.json` envelope, which puts large tables and inline data such as chat memories, notes, messages, gallery metadata, and other future bulky records under one JSON-size/memory assumption.

That makes future heavy-user profiles fragile: a single large table can make the whole profile hard to read, validate, preview, back up, import safely, or partially recover.

## Proposed behavior

Add a next-generation profile export/import format that can scale beyond one huge inline JSON document while preserving backward compatibility with current exports.

The format should define a clear manifest and per-table or chunked record contract, for example:

- A manifest with profile version, app version, exported table list, counts, byte sizes, and compatibility metadata.
- Separate files or chunks for large record groups such as chats, messages, memories, notes, assets/index data, and settings.
- Streaming or staged import so Marinara can validate and report planned changes before destructive replacement.
- Per-table normalization/validation hooks so legacy field-shape fixes do not only live in one import path.
- A preflight summary that makes destructive import behavior clear before the user commits.
- Backward-compatible support for current v1 `marinara-profile.json` exports.

## Expected owner or impact area

- [ ] App shell, navigation, startup, or providers
- [x] Catalog resources: chats, characters, personas, lorebooks, presets, connections, agents, gallery, or knowledge
- [ ] Chat mode
- [ ] Roleplay mode

- [ ] Professor Mari or shell tools
- [x] React-free engine behavior, contracts, agents, or capability ports
- [x] Shared API wrapper or remote runtime routing
- [x] Tauri/Rust storage, assets, LLM, integrations, security, imports, or HTTP runtime
- [x] Docs, contributor workflow, or templates

## Refactor branch considerations

- Do not solve this only by raising profile JSON size limits.
- Preserve import compatibility for current exports and any legacy profiles already in the wild.
- Keep destructive import confirmation explicit and data-specific.
- Validate current and legacy record shapes at the import/storage boundary, not only in UI.
- Consider remote-runtime and Tauri desktop paths separately so the format does not assume one host transport.
- Keep the first implementation slice small enough to review, likely starting with a documented v2 manifest/chunk contract plus read-only preflight.

## Alternatives considered

- Keep increasing the monolithic JSON read cap: rejected because it delays the same failure mode and does not improve validation, preview, or recovery.
- Keep the current format and rely on manual backups: insufficient because the app owns the destructive import workflow and should make large-profile risks visible.
- Split only `chats.memories`: potentially a good first slice, but the format should be designed so other large record groups can use the same contract later.

## Additional context

Related issues:

- #1511 fixed the immediate heavy-profile import cap failure.
- #1512 covered clearer confirmation for destructive profile import.
- #1513 covered legacy lorebook-entry field normalization during import.

## Summary

Generic storage writes can still persist malformed `lorebook-entries` records even though the legacy import path now normalizes string booleans and JSON-like arrays.

## Expected behavior

Every subsystem that writes `lorebook-entries` should cross one strong record-shape contract. Boolean, array, number, metadata, timing, and scope fields should either be normalized to the native shape or rejected before they reach persistent storage, regardless of whether the row came from the editor, bulk creation, import, tool-generated entries, remote runtime, or another generic storage caller.

## Actual behavior

The legacy import path was fixed for #1513, but the generic storage boundary remains loosely typed. Source audit against `upstream/refactor` found:

- `src/features/catalog/lorebooks/hooks/use-lorebooks.ts` creates, updates, copies, moves, reorders, and bulk-creates lorebook entries through `storageApi` with `Record<string, unknown>` / `unknown[]` payloads.
- `src/shared/api/storage-api.ts` normalizes stored JSON for chats and messages, but does not normalize `lorebook-entries`.
- `src/engine/contracts/schemas/lorebook.schema.ts` exports `createLorebookEntrySchema` and `updateLorebookEntrySchema`, but current grep found no active call sites using those schemas at the write boundary.
- Native import normalization in `src-tauri/src/commands/storage/imports/normalization.rs` handles legacy lorebook fields, but that does not protect later generic `storage_create` / `storage_update` calls.

That means a future or existing caller that bypasses the fixed legacy import path can still hand strings like `"false"` or JSON strings like `"[\"moon\"]"` across the storage boundary and rely on downstream UI/generation code to guess the intended shape.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Use a generic storage write path such as `storage_create` / `storage_update` for entity `lorebook-entries`.
2. Send a malformed but plausible legacy-style payload, for example `enabled: "false"`, `constant: "true"`, `keys: "[\"moon\"]"`, or `secondaryKeys: "[]"`.
3. Read the row through the lorebook editor, active lorebook scan, or `search_lorebook` tooling.
4. Observe that the row shape depends on caller-side assumptions instead of one enforced storage/lorebook-entry contract.

## Impact area

## Summary

Reimporting a character's embedded lorebook creates a new linked lorebook every time instead of updating/reusing the existing linked lorebook.

## Expected behavior

After a character's embedded lorebook has been imported once, clicking "Reimport Embedded Lorebook" or calling `character_embedded_lorebook_import` again should either update/replace the existing linked lorebook or clearly ask before creating a duplicate. The API's `reimported` field should accurately reflect the behavior.

## Actual behavior

Native Tauri QA created a character with one embedded `character_book` entry. The first `character_embedded_lorebook_import` call created and linked a lorebook correctly. A second call created a second lorebook for the same character, moved the character metadata pointer to the new lorebook, left the previous lorebook behind, and still returned `reimported: false`.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Create or import a character whose `data.character_book.entries` contains at least one entry.
2. Import the embedded lorebook from the character Lorebook tab, or call `character_embedded_lorebook_import` for that character id.

4. Import/reimport the embedded lorebook again.
5. Query lorebooks where `characterId` or `sourceCharacterId` is the character id.
6. Observe multiple linked lorebooks for the same embedded book, while the API reports `reimported: false`.

## Summary

The built-in `search_lorebook` tool still searches every stored lorebook entry, so disabled or out-of-scope lorebooks can be returned to tool-using agents.

## Expected behavior

`search_lorebook` should only return entries that are allowed for the active chat/generation context, or its contract should clearly distinguish a global library search from active lorebook retrieval. Disabled lorebooks, disabled folders, and unrelated chat/character/persona scopes should not leak into agent tool results by default.

## Actual behavior

Native Tauri QA on `origin/refactor` showed `search_lorebook` returning an entry from a disabled lorebook when `activatedLorebookEntries` was empty. Source inspection matches the behavior: `src/engine/generation/tools-runtime.ts` loads all `lorebook-entries`, merges them with activated entries, and scores them without checking the parent lorebook enabled/scope/folder state.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Create or seed a disabled lorebook with an enabled entry whose content contains a unique marker.
2. In a persisted chat, call the built-in `search_lorebook` tool with a query matching that marker and an empty `activatedLorebookEntries` input.
3. Observe that the disabled lorebook entry is returned with `source: "stored"`.

Found during the 2026-05-29 native Tauri Lorebooks QA/code-path audit on `origin/refactor` commit `f120eb33`.

## What happened

Lorebook entry timing controls are exposed in the editor and stored on entries, but the runtime prompt activation path does not persist or reuse timing state. `ephemeral` appears to be saved/normalized but not consumed by activation at all.

## Expected

- `sticky` keeps an entry active for N messages after it triggers.
- `cooldown` prevents immediate reactivation until N messages pass.
- `delay` waits N messages before first activation and then allows activation once the delay state counts down.
- `ephemeral` auto-disables or decrements per chat after N activations, matching the type comment for per-chat overrides.

## Actual

The active prompt path calls `scanForActivatedEntries(...)` without passing `timingStates`, and no generation/prompt path found by source search calls `updateTimingStatesForScan(...)` or writes `chat.metadata.entryTimingStates` / `entryStateOverrides` after activation.

Consequences from the current code path:

- `sticky` has no prior state to keep an entry active.
- `cooldown` has no persisted state, so activations are not throttled across turns.
- `delay` entries can be blocked forever because the delay state is never initialized/decremented by the runtime path.
- `ephemeral` is normalized from storage but not checked or decremented by `scanForActivatedEntries(...)`.

## Evidence

Relevant code paths inspected:

- `src/engine/generation/prompt-assembly.ts` normalizes `sticky`, `cooldown`, `delay`, and `ephemeral`, then calls `scanForActivatedEntries(...)` without timing-state options.
- `src/engine/generation-core/lorebooks/keyword-scanner.ts` defines `updateTimingStatesForScan(...)`, but repo search found no runtime caller.
- `src/engine/contracts/types/chat.ts` defines `entryStateOverrides` and `entryTimingStates`, but repo search found no prompt-generation writeback path.
- `src/features/catalog/lorebooks/components/LorebookEntryRow.tsx` exposes the Timing controls and autosaves those fields.

## Acceptance criteria

- Runtime generation loads per-chat lorebook timing state before scanning and persists the updated state after scanning.
- `sticky`, `cooldown`, and `delay` behave across turns in a focused prompt-generation test.
- `ephemeral` either receives a real per-chat decrement/disable implementation or is removed/hidden from the active behavior contract.
- Prompt preview behavior is explicit: either debug-only/no mutation, or a clear read-only projection of the current timing state.
payload.title: [Issue]: Lorebook timing controls are saved but not wired into runtime activation

Found during the 2026-05-29 native Tauri Lorebooks QA pass on `origin/refactor` commit `f120eb33`.

Proof method: seeded disposable lorebook/chat records through the app's Tauri storage API, then ran the app's own prompt-preview assembly from the native WebView. The same pass included positive controls for selected, global, character-scoped, persona-scoped, and roleplay-trigger-filtered entries.
## What happened

Lorebook token-budget controls are saved but not applied by prompt activation.

## Repro

1. Create a chat with `metadata.lorebookTokenBudget: 1`.
2. Attach multiple active lorebook entries whose combined content is well over one estimated token.
3. Run prompt preview / active world-info scan.

## Expected

The chat's lorebook token budget should limit injected lorebook entries, or the UI should not present the setting as controlling prompt activation.

## Actual

Prompt preview still injected all active lorebook entries. In QA, the preview included direct, disabled-folder, scan-depth, recursion-parent, roleplay-trigger, global, character-scoped, and persona-scoped lore markers despite the chat metadata budget being `1`.

This is distinct from #1533, which tracks tokenizer-backed estimates. This bug is about the configured budget not being read/applied at all.

## Likely owner

`src/features/modes/shared/chat-ui/components/ChatSettingsDrawer.tsx` saves `metadata.lorebookTokenBudget`, but `src/engine/generation/prompt-assembly.ts` calls:

```ts
processActivatedEntries(activated, readNumber(input.request.lorebookTokenBudget, 0));
```

The prompt-preview input and generation request schema do not appear to pass the chat metadata value into `input.request.lorebookTokenBudget`.

Per-lorebook `tokenBudget` is also saved on lorebook records, but the prompt assembly path does not use that value when processing selected books.

## Acceptance criteria

- The chat-level lorebook token budget saved in metadata is applied to prompt assembly for preview and generation, or the UI contract is changed.
- Clarify or implement per-lorebook `tokenBudget` behavior so the record field is not misleading.
- Add regression coverage proving over-budget lore entries are skipped from assembled prompts.

Found during the 2026-05-29 native Tauri Lorebooks QA pass on `origin/refactor` commit `f120eb33`.

## What happened

Lorebook-level `scanDepth` and `recursiveScanning` settings are saved but not honored by prompt activation.

## Repro A: lorebook scan depth

1. Create an active lorebook with `scanDepth: 1`.
2. Add an entry with no entry-level scan-depth override and key `LQA_OLD_KEY`.
3. Put `LQA_OLD_KEY` only in an older message, not the latest message.
4. Run prompt preview / active world-info scan.

Expected: the entry should not activate because the lorebook default scan depth should limit scanning to the latest message.
Actual: the entry activated and `LQA_SCAN_DEPTH_CONTENT_SHOULD_NOT_APPEAR` appeared in the assembled prompt.

## Repro B: recursive scanning

1. Use an active lorebook with `recursiveScanning: true`.
2. Add a parent entry triggered by chat text whose content includes the child entry's key.
3. Add a child entry triggered only by that parent content.
4. Run prompt preview.

Expected: recursive scanning should activate the child entry when recursion is enabled.
Actual: only the parent activated; `LQA_RECURSIVE_CHILD_CONTENT_SHOULD_APPEAR_IF_RECURSION_WIRED` was absent.

## Likely owner

`loadActivatedLore(...)` in `src/engine/generation/prompt-assembly.ts` normalizes flat entries and calls `scanForActivatedEntries(...)` directly. It does not apply lorebook-level `scanDepth` defaults to entries, and it does not call `recursiveScan(...)` when a selected book has `recursiveScanning: true`.

## Acceptance criteria

- Entry activation honors the selected lorebook's default `scanDepth` for entries without an entry-level override.
- Recursive scanning is either wired for lorebooks with `recursiveScanning: true`, or the UI/storage contract is changed so the setting is not presented as active behavior.
- Add focused regression tests for lorebook-level scan depth and recursive activation.

The refactor branch now has registered prompt overrides for `conversation.selfie`, including the Settings editor and import normalization for the supported key. Legacy prompt override support was broader and included image-generation surfaces beyond conversation selfies.

## What problem does this solve?

Tracker state currently has durable IDs for top-level tracker entities such as `PresentCharacter.characterId` and `QuestProgress.questEntryId`, but nested list rows are still reconciled by visible keys such as `name` or `text`.

That visible-key fallback is better than pure index-based merging, but duplicate labels remain ambiguous. Examples include two stats named `HP`, duplicate inventory item names, repeated custom field names, or quest objectives with the same text. In those cases, manual UI patches and agent snapshot merges can still target the wrong nested row.

## Proposed behavior

Add stable durable IDs for nested tracker rows where list reconciliation needs identity, including:

- `CharacterStat` entries for character, player, and persona stats
- `InventoryItem` entries
- `CustomTrackerField` entries
- Quest objective rows

The implementation should define a migration/defaulting strategy for existing snapshots and generated agent output, keep legacy/no-id rows readable, and update merge helpers to prefer durable IDs while retaining the current visible-key fallback for older data.

Add focused coverage for duplicate names/text, existing no-id rows, and migrated/defaulted IDs.

## Summary

## Expected behavior

The hide/collapse summary settings should behave consistently across summary paths:

- Manual `last N` summary generation should persist settings and hide selected source messages when enabled.

At minimum, the UI should clearly label JSONL export/import as transcript-only if avatars and character links are intentionally unsupported.

Current-code audit shows the JSONL export path writes message rows only, while the ST JSONL import path creates a new chat with empty `characterIds` and imports each message with `characterId: null` and `extra: {}`.

That means the imported transcript has no stable source for character avatars even if the original chat had character cards and avatar paths.

1. **Delete-all wording (decided behavior).** Per the #1519 review: a branch group's "delete all" intentionally removes the whole group including the original chat, which makes branched groups consistent with ST-imported groups (whose root is already a group member and already deleted by `delete_chat_group`). The remaining issue is labels:
   - `src/app/shell/ChatSidebar.tsx` delete dialog (around lines 1216 and 1243): "This conversation has {n} branches" / "Delete All {n} Branches" now counts the root as a branch and implies the original survives.
   - `src/features/modes/shared/chat-ui/components/ChatFilesDrawer.tsx` "Delete All Branches" footer button: same implication.
   Reword to match the behavior (e.g. "Delete entire group" / "Delete all {n} chats" / "{n} chats in this group"), keeping terminology consistent across `ChatFilesDrawer`, `ChatBranchSelector`, and `ChatSidebar`. The deletion itself is correct; only the copy needs to align.

2. **No migration for already-branched chats.** #1519 only enrolls the root for chats branched after the fix. Profiles that already have branches whose root stayed `groupId: null` are not retroactively repaired, so Manage Chat Files still shows the no-group state from those roots. A one-time migration (for each chat that is the target of some other chat's `groupId`, set its own `groupId` to that id when currently null) would repair existing data.
payload.title: Branch groups: delete dialog counts the root as a branch, and existing ungrouped roots are not migrated

payload.author: Romuromylus
payload.body:
Follow-up to #1512 (fixed for the legacy table path in #1518).

#1518 made the **legacy** import path (`fileStorage.tables`) skip-absent: a collection whose table key is missing from the file is left untouched instead of wiped. The **modern** `data.collections` import path (`src-tauri/src/commands/storage/profile.rs`, `import_profile_collections_with_restored_assets`) still rebuilds replacements for every mapped collection and falls back to an empty array for ones absent from the file, so a partial modern-format profile would still wipe the collections it omits.

In practice the refactor's own exports are always full backups, so this is not triggered by a normal export/import round-trip. But a hand-built or partial modern-format file has the same data-loss shape #1512 described for the legacy path.

Suggested: apply the same present-key guard to the modern collections path so absent collections are left untouched, while present-but-empty still clears.
payload.title: Profile import: modern collections path still full-replaces collections absent from the file
